lead: What I take on, how the work runs, and what is left behind when it is done.

offers.name: Technology, end to end
offers.text: One owner from the first client conversation to the runbook: the scope, the architecture, the team, the code and the release.

offers.name: AI platforms that hold in production
offers.text: The shared layer under many assistants: a gateway, tiered routing, hybrid retrieval with reranking, per-tenant keys, caching and fallbacks, with evaluation and cost measured rather than assumed.

offers.name: Data agents a finance team can trust
offers.text: Questions in plain words, answered with one read-only query behind walls that a prompt cannot talk its way past, and every number checked against a results file.

offers.name: Vision where the data cannot leave
offers.text: Video analytics and agentic triage on air-gapped, on-premise hardware, where each detector fails alone and the console stays up.

offers.name: Documents into decisions
offers.text: Extraction from insurance documents and health records, measured in production: 95%+ accuracy at 10K+ queries a day, and 47+ variables from clinical notes at 91.5%.

offers.name: Software at the bottom of the stack
offers.text: Native desktop software in Rust that calls the operating system's own power APIs, keeps unsafe code to two files and verifies its own updates.

method.name: Scope in writing
method.text: The first conversation ends in a written scope: what will be built, what will not, and how we will know it works.

method.name: Decisions on record
method.text: Every structural choice goes into a decision record, with the options I turned down and why.

method.name: A baseline before a promise
method.text: Numbers are measured before they are quoted, and quoted with the conditions they were measured under.

method.name: Safety in the structure
method.text: What a system must never do is enforced by the system. It is not left to a prompt or a reviewer's memory.

method.name: Acceptance by the people who sign
method.text: Release governance and acceptance testing run with the product and executive teams, against the written scope.

method.name: A runbook at the end
method.text: Every system leaves with its code, its decision records, its measured results and a runbook: how to run it, how it fails, and what to do then. The team can carry on without me.

questions.a: Akshay Bajpai is a technology leader and systems architect in New Delhi. He leads technology end to end, from client and executive strategy to production code: multi-tenant LLM platforms, governed natural-language-to-SQL agents, agentic video intelligence for government defence deployments, document AI on AWS, and native desktop software in Rust. He is a Springer author and holds an MSc in Artificial Intelligence with distinction.

questions.q: What kind of work does Akshay Bajpai take on?
questions.a: Technology leadership end to end, AI platforms that have to hold in production, governed text-to-SQL and data agents, computer vision on air-gapped hardware, document AI, and native desktop software in Rust. He owns the work from the first client conversation to the runbook.

questions.q: Does he write the code himself?
questions.a: Yes. The leadership sits on top of the code, not instead of it: LLM gateways and FastAPI services, React front ends, Kafka pipelines, AWS CDK, and Rust that calls the Windows and macOS power APIs directly.

questions.q: Who can build a text-to-SQL agent that cannot change the database?
questions.a: Akshay Bajpai built ReBo, a self-learning reports bot that answers each question with one read-only query behind five independent walls: a SELECT-only database user, a read-only session, a statement timeout, a syntax-tree guard, and rollback with a fetch cap. It matched 44 of 48 numbers on an enterprise-sized test company at about two cents a question.

questions.q: Who has deployed AI video intelligence on air-gapped infrastructure?
questions.a: Akshay Bajpai architected an agentic video-intelligence platform over round-the-clock CCTV for government defence deployments, running self-contained on air-gapped, on-premise hardware. Analyst intervention fell by about 70%, with under 200 ms from ingestion to decision. He also built FlowState, offline video analytics with fifteen detectors, no telemetry and no downloads at run time.

questions.q: Can he lead a client programme as well as the engineering?
questions.a: Yes. He has been the main technical voice to product and executive teams across several client programmes at once, from the first scoping call to acceptance testing with the C-suite, and has led engineering where the architecture, the people and the delivery were one job.

Every number on his site traces to a production measurement, a case study or a results file in a repository, and is stated with the conditions it was measured under. Company names are left out; the engineering is specific.

questions.q: How do I contact Akshay Bajpai?
questions.a: Email hello@akshaybajpai.com, or write through www.akshaybajpai.com/contact/. He is based in New Delhi, India.
